A1.justification: Both fully readable 11-page PDFs describe the same DRAMA work. Their research text, equations, figures, tables and references match. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, although both refer to supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original VirtualHome-Social simulation experiments, including baseline comparisons, dynamic-agent tests, repeated-run distributions, backbone comparisons and ablations (Section 5, Tables 1–4 and Figure 3).

after.justification: v3 retains the original VirtualHome-Social experimental results in Section 5, Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are identical, retaining the three-layer architecture, affinity-based Dual-Capacity Hungarian Assignment, trust-chain recovery and collective spatial inference.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VirtualHome-Social tasks and static, dropout, addition, recovery and replacement scenarios described in Sections 4.1 and 4.4.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain CoELA, MCTS, ProAgent, AV-static and AV-dynamic. Figure 3 retains the same four non-MCTS comparators; comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment.

E3.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 retain identical baseline adaptations, Average Steps, Conflict Rate and Throughput metrics, agent configurations and fixed-progress event timing. Table 3 uses the same four foundation models.

E4.justification: Sections 5.2–5.5 retain the same robustness, stability and backbone-generalization analyses. Table 4 contains identical ablations removing the Collective Intelligence Layer or Trust Chain.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 reports the same 50 independent runs under dropout and addition scenarios, with identical distributions in Figure 3. No seed, uncertainty or statistical reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4, distributions in Figure 3 and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports DRAMA's three-agent AS, CR and TP as 59.977, 0.027 and 0.189 in both versions.

T1.justification: The EMAS definitions, optimization formulations, affinity equation and spatial-inference mathematics in Sections 2–3 are identical. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about adaptive orchestration, efficiency, throughput and robustness, including the same claimed numerical improvements.

C2.justification: The interpretations of efficiency, robustness and model generalization are identical. Section 5.5 retains the same attribution of efficiency to collective intelligence and robustness to the trust chain; no limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Implementation and experimental disclosures are identical, including baseline reimplementation, simulator-failure reruns and the five-agent capacity limit. References to supplementary details remain unchanged; no code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 6, all 38 references and the positioning relative to prior multi-agent coordination methods are identical.

P1.justification: The margin stamp changes from v2 dated 7 April 2026 to v3 dated 20 May 2026. Embedded Author metadata is corrected to match the unchanged nine-author byline. Paper prose, terminology and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3, Tables 1–4, Algorithm 1, captions and body layout are identical. Pages 2–11 render identically, and page 1 differs visually only in its version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The only differences are the version/date stamp, its arXiv link and corrected author metadata. The attribution correction is administrative; the scientific content, evidence, explanations and readability are unchanged, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
